chicken-breast-baked-or-broiled-skin-not.title: Chicken breast, baked or broiled, skin not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Skinless chicken breast is a lean source of protein obtained from the fillet of a chicken, prepared by baking or broiling without added fat. It is commonly served in fast‑food outlets and restaurants as a standalone piece or as part of a dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken breast provides about 31 g of protein per 100 g.
When baked without skin, fat content drops to less than 2 g per 100 g.
Chicken meat is a good source of vitamin B6, which supports amino‑acid metabolism.
In the United States, chicken breast ranks among the top‑10 most popular fast‑food items.
Proper cooking retains moisture in the muscle fibers, keeping the breast juicy.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: Protein is essential for tissue growth, repair, and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Low fat
items.content: Skin‑less preparation makes it suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamin B6 and niacin support energy metabolism and nervous‑system health.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Chicken breast supplies phosphorus, selenium, and zinc, important for bones and immunity.

items.title: Supports muscle mass
items.content: Rich in essential amino acids, especially leucine, which stimulates muscle‑protein synthesis.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Undercooked chicken may contain Salmonella; cook to an internal temperature of 75 °C.

items.title: Bird‑meat allergy
items.content: A small number of people can have allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: High sodium in restaurant versions
items.content: Fast‑food chicken breasts are often brined, increasing sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chicken breast can be sliced and added to salads, sandwiches, wraps, or used in dishes like pasta and rice. In restaurants it is often served with sauces; choosing lighter sauce options is advisable.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store raw breast in the refrigerator at ≤ 4 °C for no more than 2 days. Cooked breast can be kept in an airtight container for up to 3 days or frozen for up to 3 months.

content.title: About
content.content: Ritz Peanut Butter Filled Crackers are crunchy whole‑grain biscuits sandwiched with a sweet‑salty peanut butter filling. They are convenient for on‑the‑go snacking and offer a creamy, slightly sweet flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The snack is produced by Nabisco, the maker of the classic Ritz brand.
The peanut butter filling contains a modest amount of sugar and salt to balance flavor.
Each cracker is individually wrapped, making it popular in school lunches and travel packs.
The original recipe uses toasted whole‑grain wheat for added fiber.
These crackers are often used in kids' lunchboxes as a quick, portable snack.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: The peanut butter provides about 5 g of protein per 30 g serving, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: Peanuts are rich in monounsaturated fats, which can be heart‑friendly when consumed in moderation.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The snack supplies niacin and folate, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain crackers add a modest amount of dietary fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: The combination of carbs and fats provides fast‑acting energy, useful during active days.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: The peanut butter filling can trigger severe allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High sugar and salt
items.content: Regular consumption may contribute to excess sugar and sodium intake.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: These crackers are relatively calorie‑dense; portion control is advised for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Possible trans fats
items.content: Some formulations may contain small amounts of trans fats; check the label if this is a concern.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the crackers straight from the pack as a quick snack. They also work well in lunchboxes, as a base for mini open‑face sandwiches, or paired with fruit for a balanced bite.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, reseal the package tightly to maintain crispness. Discard if you notice off‑flavors or signs of spoilage.

content.title: About
content.content: Flavored Martini is a ready‑to‑drink alcoholic beverage based on gin and vermouth, enhanced with natural flavorings such as berries, citrus or herbs. It has a characteristic dry taste with a hint of sweetness and aromatic aftertaste, suitable for sipping neat or using in cocktails.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first flavored Martini appeared in the 1970s as a response to growing demand for lighter, aromatic drinks.
There are more than 20 flavor variants: lemon, raspberry, strawberry, cucumber, rosemary, etc.
Martini is a key ingredient in classic cocktails like the Martini Julep, Vodka Martini and Martini with tonic.
The "Martini" brand was registered in Italy in 1863 and has become synonymous with premium vermouth.
Flavored versions often contain less sugar than the traditional sweet vermouth.

items.title: Moderate consumption may promote relaxation
items.content: Small amounts of alcohol have a calming effect, reducing stress and improving mood.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Natural flavorings (berries, citrus) are rich in polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: May support cardiovascular health when consumed moderately
items.content: Studies suggest moderate vermouth intake can improve blood lipid profiles.

items.title: Alcohol‑related risk
items.content: Excessive intake leads to intoxication, impaired coordination and long‑term health issues.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Alcohol can amplify the effects of sedatives, anticoagulants and certain antibiotics.

items.title: Not recommended for pregnant or nursing women
items.content: Alcohol may adversely affect fetal development and lactation.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Some flavored versions contain added sugar, which is important for people with diabetes.

content.title: How to Drink
content.content: Serve flavored Martini chilled in a martini glass or use it as a cocktail base. Add ice, an olive, lemon zest or fresh berries to enhance the flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the bottle in a cool, dark place with the cap tightly sealed. After opening, it is best consumed within 3–6 months to preserve aroma and taste.
